'A special occasion': Grand final mindset driving Bulldogs to finish on high
The Bulldogs’ finals hopes may be over, but Cameron Ciraldo isn’t letting his side’s final game of the season be treated as a dead rubber.
Instead, Canterbury are treating Thursday night’s clash with Brisbane at Accor Stadium as their own grand final, determined to finish the year with one last performance for their fans at home.
While the game may have little impact on the finals picture, Ciraldo has made a conscious effort to turn the Bulldogs’ final week of the season into a special occasion.
Jacob Preston Try
The players took part in their final captain’s run at Accor Stadium, a reminder of the privilege of playing in the NRL and an opportunity to soak in their home ground one last time before the season comes to an end.
“Any game you get to play in the NRL, especially at a stadium like this, is a privilege and we should be grateful,” Ciraldo said.
“We train out here quite a bit; it’s our home ground and we mix it up at times during the season.
“We thought today, it’s our last game here, the field’s in great shape and we’re trying to make it a special occasion.”

Despite missing the finals for the first time in three years, Ciraldo said he remained proud of the way his players had continued to fight.
“There has been a lot of learning this year and the way we finished the season, I’ve been really proud of our guys,” he said.
“We finished a couple of wins behind where we would have liked to and we can pinpoint where they were.
“We played some great footy along the way.”
And while some may label the final-round clash a dead rubber, Ciraldo was not a fan of that description.
Captain Critta seals the deal
“There are no dead rubbers. It’s an NRL game,” he said.
“These guys have been dreaming of playing NRL since they were five years old and for our fans, it’s no dead rubber.
“Everything we have done this week is about putting our best performance in tomorrow night and the way the guys have prepared gives me confidence in that.”
The final game will also provide an opportunity for the Bulldogs to reflect on a season that included plenty of change.
One of the biggest talking points was the positional switch of star centre Stephen Crichton into the halves alongside young playmaker Lachlan Galvin.
Since Ciraldo moved Crichton into the No.6 jersey, the results began to turn.
“Over the next couple of weeks we will review that as a playing group and staff and go through what could have been and what we needed to be better at,” he said.
“There might be 16 teams sitting back at the end of the season thinking they failed. It depends how you want to view it.”

items.body_excerpt:
Last ride: Patty and Payne vowing to go out on a high
Pat Carrigan is determined to give best mate Payne Haas the send-off he deserves against the Bulldogs on Thursday night.
The end of the season can't come quickly for the Broncos, who have mustered just seven wins on the way to becoming the first defending premiers in 20 years to miss the NRL finals.
For Haas and Carrigan, who came through the ranks together as Broncos Under 20s players before scaling the heights in their NRL careers, the last ride comes fittingly at the ground where they shared premiership glory in 2025.
Haas made the announcement in February that he was leaving Red Hill in 2027 to join forces at Souths with Wayne Bennett, the man who handed him his NRL debut back in 2018.
Related Signings
Haas to leave Broncos for Souths in one of game's biggest coups
“Obviously, personally he's one of my best mates,” Carrigan said.
“We came in as kids here and been through a lot of adversity and grown both on-and-off the field together too, so our relationship will extend long past these four walls.
“But I think for the club and for the game – I don't even know how many Paul Morgan Medals (Broncos NRLM player of the year awards) he's won but he's definitely well clear.
"I think (it’s) him and Alf – his legacy and the standards that he's set around the place I can see in all the younger boys and that's the testament of his mark on this place.
Pat Carrigan and Payne Haas celebrate a win over the Bulldogs in 2020. ©Scott Davis / NRL Images
“We started our journey together, but hey that's life...
“In my opinion, he's the best front-rower in the game, so I know it's hard to replace with one person, but they've probably have done a good job with recruitment and guys like Mitch Barnett, Xavier Willison ... great additions to the club."
As he prepares to sign off after 159 games as a Bronco, Haas was full of praise for Carrigan's leadership qualities.
"Everyone sees what he does on the field, but I think off the field, the way he carries himself, the way he speaks, he gives us lots of confidence on the field and off the field as well," Haas said.
“(He is) someone I have looked up to during my career and the way you hold yourself, I try to hold myself in that way as well."
Asked what he would miss most about the Broncos after giving his heart and soul to the club for a decade, Haas said simply, "just the boys, to be honest".
Payne Haas is everywhere
“Obviously this club's a very special club and we get looked after, but I think more the connection with the boys and the way we get along.
“Everyone's united and (that's) something I'm going to really miss.
“(I am) just trying to enjoy this week and really enjoy the time with these boys.
“I remember coming in a bit raw and I got in a bit of trouble the first few years of my career, but if it wasn't for the Broncos... I wouldn’t be a better man and especially the footy player I am, it's because of them.”

The Broncos can’t make finals, but there’s still everything to play for.
Especially if your name is Ben Hunt, with the veteran set to run out in the No.7 jersey in a huge audition under Michael Maguire.
A three-way battle is set to take place ahead of the 2027 season for Brisbane’s coveted halfback spot — and Hunt will be desperate to put his best foot forward against the Bulldogs on Thursday night.
Come March next year, Hunt will be 37-years-old and competing with two players more than a decade his junior on Tom Duffy and recruit Jonah Pezet.
Duffy shown glimpses of promise this season and was handed a fresh contract until the end of 2028 in June, while Hunt himself signed on for a further season.
That decision was met with heavy scrutiny, but speaking to Code Sports , Hunt has declared he is gunning to wear the No.7 next season.
“I’m a competitor and I’ve always made it clear the No.7 is my favourite jersey,” he said.
“If the coaches decide that that’s not to be, then that’s not to be.
“But I’ll still fight hard every week to get in there and play that position because that’s what I love.
“That’s where I want to play next year.”

The 23-year-old was signed to be the heir to Adam Reynolds’ throne, with Brisbane bosses hopeful time in the Eels’ starting side would assist in his develop.

items.snippet: ‘It stinks’: Luai twist after blindsiding Tigers with PNG trip    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
NRL great Corey Parker has whacked Jarome Luai ’s trip to PNG last weekend, as the outgoing Wests Tigers captain prepares for a farewell game.
Luai limped off during the side’s round 26 loss against the Cowboys with a leg injury, but has been cleared to play in the final round of the season. On Tuesday afternoon he was named in the Tigers side to play against his former club Penrith, wearing the No.6 jersey (scroll below for all the NRL round 27 team lists).
Jarome Luai poses with PNG Prime Minister James Marape. Challenger PGA Tour of Australasia
After his side’s loss to the Cowboys on Saturday, Luai and the rest of the Tigers players were given time off, with the five-eighth asking if he could stay back in Townsville.
One day later, photos surfaced online of Luai at a golf event in Port Moresby, rubbing shoulders with PNG Prime Minister James Marape. The Sydney Morning Herald reports that some Tigers officials learned of the trip via social media.
It comes after Luai was unveiled as the official face of Pepsi in the country ahead of his big-money, long-term move to the Chiefs in 2028.
“This is a team that he’s going to be representing in two years’ time,” Broncos great Parker said on SENQ Breakfast on Tuesday.
“He’s at the Eels next year, he’s still a contracted Tigers player. He was brought to the Tigers to be the saviour, to turn the culture around and lead. He was all on board saying ‘I’m in here for the long haul’ and then he got out of it.
Read more
‘Don’t see that happening’: Gus puts Cleary to PNG rumours to bed
“I think it stinks. To be fair, he’s not breaking any rules – but I don’t like it.”
In other team news, the Roosters have taken an incredibly cautious approach after the injury to halfback Sam Walker ruled him out for the season.
South Sydney will again trot out Latrell Mitchell in a bid to gain more match fitness, while the struggling Sharks have rested some high-profile players.
For clubs in the bottom-half of the ladder, the Raiders will debut a highly-touted playmaker, while Broncos fans will get a look at a young gun.
St George Illawarra will farewell a host of Super League-bound stars as they look to end a disappointing 2026 campaign on a positive note.
